pr.title: Move a single-file store into a package, and merge later saves to it
pr.head: 608225d28f291e05c7e61340786eb72083b7168a

summary: multipass keeps a password store encrypted with age under one passphrase. Earlier releases kept it in a single file, ~/.multipass/store.age. The layer below this one replaces that file with a package: a folder, store.multipass, holding a key file under the passphrase and store files under a random vault key. That layer refuses to open a single-file store, so anyone upgrading would be stuck.

This pull request moves a single-file store into a package at its first passphrase prompt. It leaves the old file in place, because another Mac still on an older multipass may keep saving to it, and at each later prompt it merges any such save into the package. Once the old file has gone 30 days unchanged, multipass deletes it. A small record inside the package, the move record, remembers what the old file held so that a later change to it can be told apart.

The merged changes carry stamps that every Mac computes the same way, so a change merged twice, by two Macs or after a crash, changes nothing the second time. When a passwd left the old file under the earlier passphrase, the prompt asks for that passphrase. An old file in a folder that cannot be written is read as it is. It is the last layer of the vault-key plan, so it also marks that plan completed and records what the build settled.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Old file: the single-file store from before the package, normally ~/.multipass/store.age.
  • Package: the store.multipass folder of key and store files.
  • Move record: moved.<gen>.<id>.age in the package, under the vault key. It holds the old file's name, the SHA-256 of its bytes, when that hash was recorded (since), and a snapshot of the old store's text.
  • Stamp: an entry's modified time in milliseconds. When two copies of the store merge, the entry with the later stamp wins.
  • Retirement: deleting the old file and then its records, once the file has gone 30 days unchanged.

cards.title: Review status at this head
cards.html:
The review of 608225d is clean, and the head is signed off, with no suggestions standing. The three findings from earlier heads are fixed and resolved: a change re-applied by a second Mac, --store naming a retired old file, and saves under the passphrase before a passwd. Both later suggestions are in place: passwd and rekey no longer ask for the old file's passphrase, and the docs describe the one stamping case that remains. The head merges the moved vault-key-format branch, with main's installer and multipass upgrade, and README counts about 4,000 lines outside the cryptography.

All repository checks pass locally. CI's test job was still running at publication.

groups.title: The move and the old-file check
groups.kicker: How src/vault.rs builds the package from the old file and checks that file at every later prompt
intro: Vault::open_or_move decides between opening the package and moving the old file into one. It moves only when the package folder does not exist and the old file does. move_in asks for the passphrase, decrypts the old file, and builds the package in store.multipass.tmp with a key file, one store file, and a move record, then renames the folder into place, so the package appears whole or not at all. The old file is never written. When the folder cannot be written, move_in returns the old store read-only, as Opened::Unmoved.
Every later prompt that can write runs Session::settle, which calls check_old_file after any rotation. That function groups the move records by old file and compares the file's SHA-256 with them:

What it findsWhat it does
A record with the same hashKeeps the record that has seen the file longest and deletes the others, then retires the old file and the record once that record's since is 30 days ago
No record with the hashDecrypts the old file, merges its changes since the newest record's snapshot with Store::merge, saves, writes a new record, and deletes the records it read
Old file goneDeletes the records
No record at allAdds the old file's entries at modified 0, so only missing names are added, and writes a record

old_file_changes decides the stamps. A format 3 old file carries a stamp on each entry, so it merges as it is. Formats 1 and 2 carry none, so each entry that differs from the snapshot is stamped with the old file's modification time. Two Macs that diff against the same snapshot therefore produce the same changes, and merging them again changes nothing.

When a changed old file opens with no passphrase typed at the prompt, ask_for_old_files asks for its passphrase (Ask::OldFile), as after a passwd. A rotation writes each move record again under the new key. hex_digest in src/crypto/sha256.rs gives the hash as hex. The old file's bytes are ciphertext, so the hash is public and compared with an ordinary ==.

checks.text: Several Macs share the package through a sync service, which brings over new files and deletions in any order. Hold that in mind at each step of check_old_file: another Mac may still see a record this Mac has already replaced. The stamping also relies on the sync service keeping the old file's modification time, as iCloud Drive does.

Two package copies, where Mac A merges an older multipass's save and the user then edits the same entry on A, end with the edit, both when Mac B holds both records and when it holds only the replaced one. A second open of each changes nothing. Checked with scratch unit tests at this head.

files.note: Adds MoveRecord, the move (open_or_move, move_in, build), check_old_file in settle, old_file_changes, ask_for_old_files, records in rotate, and tests for every format, stale and duplicate records, crashes during the move and during the merge, a format 3 file's own stamps, and the passphrase before a passwd.

checks.text: One case remains, and this docstring and plan § 2.6 say so. A Mac that missed the record of an earlier save to a format 1 or 2 old file diffs against an older snapshot. It stamps that save's changes with a later save's time, and can revert an edit made in the package between the two saves.

After a passwd and a save by main's build under the earlier passphrase, a release build asks Old file's passphrase: , merges with the answer, and lists the new entry, and the old file retires 30 days later. Checked with expect and a scratch unit test.

files.note: Adds hex_digest, the SHA-256 of a byte slice as lower-case hex, for public data only. The FIPS 180-4 vector test now checks it too.

groups.title: Finding the old file from the command line
groups.kicker: How src/main.rs maps --store, MULTIPASS_STORE, and the default path to a package and an old file
intro: package_path returns a Place: the package, the old file it was or will be moved from, and whether the user named that old file. When --store or MULTIPASS_STORE names a file, the package is the same path ending in .multipass. It stays so after the file is retired, when the path is gone and that package exists. Without either, the package is ~/.multipass/store.multipass and the old file is ~/.multipass/store.age.

run prints note: … moved to …; update MULTIPASS_STORE or --store while the user still names the old file and its package exists. open_with prints Moved … into … after a move. When the old file cannot be moved, a read command warns and reads it as it is, and a saving command fails. It prints the session's warnings after settle. open answers Ask::OldFile with an Old file's passphrase: prompt. init refuses while the old file exists, because any other command moves it.
multipass upgrade, from the base, is dispatched before run, so none of this store-path handling runs for it, and upgrade refuses --store when the arguments are parsed.

files.note: Replaces the refusal of a single-file store with Place, the note: and Moved lines, the read-only fallback, the old file's passphrase prompt, and init's new refusal.

checks.text: With release builds, --store …/store.age keeps opening the package after the old file is deleted, and init refuses with a store already exists. Checked with expect.

passwd and rekey open with Settle::Skip, so this closure answers the old file's question with None, and they never ask for a passphrase whose change they would not merge. With release builds, rekey after an old-file save asked nothing extra, and the next list asked and merged. Checked with expect.
A release build pointed at a format 2 store made by main's build prints Moved … into … on the first list and the note: line afterwards, and the old file stays. Checked with expect.

groups.title: README and the vault-key plan
groups.kicker: What a user reads about the move, and how the plan records it
intro: README gains a warning beside the install and upgrade instructions: once the store is in a package, do not go back to a multipass from before the package, with multipass upgrade <version> or an older checkout, because after the old file is retired an older multipass finds no store, and its init would create a new, empty one. It also gains a paragraph on the move, and a recovery note: a store.age beside the folder is the store from before the move, so recover from the folder.

The vault-key plan moves to completed. Its § 2.6 describes the stamps every Mac computes alike and the records that retire each other, and § 7, Outcome, records the move record's fields, the old file's passphrase prompt, the read-only fallback, and the by-hand checks.

files.note: Adds the downgrade warning under Install, a paragraph on the move under Use, and the recovery note.
Marks the plan completed, revises § 2.6, and adds § 7, Outcome.
